title: Callout curation and graded response fabric
text:
Callout curation and graded response fabric

description:
Problem: Our current paging stream generates many ephemeral pages during short-lived degradations and noisy signals (e.g., transient GPU OOM spikes, regional probe flapping). This burns on-call cognitive load and obscures genuine SLO-impacting incidents. Goal: Implement a graded response fabric that curates callouts (pages/notifications) using probabilistic throttles, contextual enrichment, and an automated runbook cascade that performs safe remediation steps before escalating to human on-call.

acceptance_criteria:
Reduce P1/critical on-call pages attributable to transient noise by >= 40% in the first 30 days
New fabric must annotate alerts with causal context (region, model, model-variant, request-path, recent rollout flag, KB id) in >95% of cases
Automated first-responder playbooks execute non-destructive remediation (restart pool, failover read-only cache, route to standby region) with explicit audit logs and can be safely disabled per-customer/route
Rollout plan (canary) deployed to 2 non-prod regions and 1 low-traffic prod region without increasing page volume during dry-run
Dashboard with pre/post signals (pages/hour, mean-page-noise, %pages-automated, MTTR) created and linked

design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
Use probabilistic throttling (token-bucket + weighted probability) so high-confidence SLO breaches bypass throttles while low-confidence signals are sampled down — favors recall for critical violations and precision for noisy signals.
Enrichment will pull from runtime trace store and model-metadata service. Trade-off: enrichment adds ~30-70ms to pipeline but provides vital context to reduce escalation churn.
Automated runbooks will be limited to safe, idempotent actions for initial rollout (eg. pod recycle, kv-cache clear, reroute to hotspot-backend). More invasive repairs (schema migrations, customer data changes) require human approval.
Per-customer and per-route overrides allow Enterprise customers to opt out of automation for compliance-sensitive workloads.
Circuit-breakers at two layers: request-level (soft CB with hinting) and region-level (hard CB for evacuations). Soft CBs are advisory and feed into throttles; hard CBs are strict and trigger traffic steering. Complexity vs safety balance prioritized towards safety.

implementation_notes:
Core components: 1) Alert Curator service (rules engine + probabilistic filter); 2) Enrichment layer (aggregate traces/metadata); 3) Runbook Composer (declarative playbooks with safety gates); 4) Orchestration agent (executes, logs, and reports). We'll integrate with PagerDuty/Slack and Redwood Console alert sinks. Storage: playbook audit events go to infra-events topic and are visible in Console runbook trace panel.

rollout_plan:
1) Unit tests + simulation harness (inject synthetic noise patterns) — complete. 2) Deploy to staging, run chaos scenarios (noise bursts, KV thrash) and validate throttling behavior — in progress. 3) Canary in low-traffic prod region for 72h with automation in 'observe only' mode, then enable safe actions behind feature flag. 4) Expand to remaining regions with two-week monitoring windows per region. 5) Post-rollout retrospective and tuning window.

monitoring_and_metrics:
pages_total/hour
pages_from_transients/hour (rule-tagged)
pages_automated_fraction
mean_time_to_acknowledge (by severity)
mttr_post_automation
false_positive_rate_of_throttle

safety_and_fallbacks:
All automated actions run with a dry-run audit before enabling; dry-run outputs are visible in Console.
Emergency 'panic' toggle to disable entire fabric per-region and per-organization in <30s.
Automated actions are rate-limited and idempotent; each action has an automated rollback step when possible.
Detailed runbook execution logs are shipped to S3 and linked to incident for postmortem.

comments:
2026-02-25 - Priya Nair: Kickoff meeting notes attached to design doc. Agreed to prioritize automatic non-destructive fixes first; security to review per-customer opt-outs.
2026-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Implemented core probabilistic throttle and basic enrichment; pushed simulated noise tests. Observed 52% reduction in synthetic transient pages in the harness.
2026-03-04 - Evelyn Chen (SRE): Feedback - we need explicit SLO delta thresholds before automation triggers. Suggest adding a short-lived hysteresis window (30s) to prevent action during short flapping.
2026-03-06 - Diego Martinez: Added hysteresis and adjusted probability weights by signal source (infra vs application). Updated PR with canary flag and documentation.
2026-03-09 - Security Review (Ana Rodrigues): Noted KMS boundary for audit logs; requested encryption-at-rest and access controls for runbook artifacts. Security review requested: true.
2026-03-10 - Diego Martinez: Integrated KMS for playbook artifacts and added per-customer opt-out. Preparing canary deploy to prod-eu-low-1 in observe-only mode.
Follow-ups: run scheduled simulation against multiregion failover scenarios (ENG-____ placeholder) and coordinate with Dedicated team for reserved capacity testing.
